clue.text: A ship liable to get a shaking is vulnerable to attack

indicators.note: whatever gets a shaking is jumbled up, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
taken as written, to be mixed with the following a
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vessel prone to being tossed about in a storm is an easy target for enemies.
explanation.walkthrough: The shaking applies only to 'liable' and the 'a' after it; the opening 'A' and the ship are taken as they come.
explanation.definitionFit: Something assailable can be assaulted or criticised, which is exactly being open to an attack.

clue.text: Attractive net with magic border

indicators.note: a border runs round the outside, so one word sits on either side of the other

blocks.note: taken as written, split to go round the other word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fishing or sports net decorated with an enchanting edge sounds very appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic describes a strong pull, used figuratively of a charming personality that draws people in.

clue.text: Bar person swung around in church, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so we want the spelling of a word that is spoken the same

blocks.note: a censer is the incense burner swung on chains during church services

explanation.surface: Someone is swung about in a church, which sounds like a lively wedding or a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person' looks like the thing swung, but it belongs with 'Bar': the incense vessel that is swung is not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor is an official who bars or suppresses material judged unacceptable, so a person who forbids.

clue.text: Singer's keen to rise

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: avid means eager or keen

explanation.surface: A performer is eager to climb the ladder of fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Sort of star: a sun to high fliers

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters following are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: the sun is a kind of star, which matters to those who fly high.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts travel into space, flying higher than anyone else, so they are literally high fliers.

clue.text: Overview otherwise supplied by site assessor

blocks.note: a survey is a general overview
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you will miss it'

explanation.surface: An alternative summary of a property comes from the person inspecting the site.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor inspects land or buildings and reports on their condition and value, assessing a site.

clue.text: Insight into Camus' endless trouble over a couple of points

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the name is dropped
trouble suggests disorder, so the shortened name is thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the French writer's name taken as written
two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A literary critic's insight into the endless troubles in Camus's philosophy, perhaps over a few key points.
explanation.walkthrough: Camus loses its S, CAMU is rearranged to ACUM, and the compass points E and N follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharp judgement or keen perception, the ability to see into things quickly.

clue.text: Fellow to decide about rising charges

indicators.note: turned about and rising up a down entry, the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
to see is to decide, as in 'I'll see what to do'

explanation.surface: A college fellow is deciding what to do about prices going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Fees are charges made for a service, such as a lawyer's or a school's payment.

clue.text: Pork dish for slim wives?

blocks.note: spare can mean thin or lean, as in a spare figure
a jocular term for wives, from Eve being made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion: a meat dish suitable for wives watching their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful use of ribs for wives, from the Genesis story of Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare ribs are cuts of pork rib with most of the meat trimmed off, usually roasted or barbecued.

clue.text: Dirty article left out for family member

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so those letters are taken away from the word

blocks.note: unclean is a synonym of dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grubby item has been put aside for a relative, perhaps a hand-me-down.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a relation, the brother of a parent or the husband of an aunt.

clue.text: Turbulent sea, main cause of memory loss

indicators.note: turbulent water is churned up, so the following letters are stirred into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rough voyage, the clue suggests, is chiefly what made someone forget everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief' in the surface; it is fodder, and 'cause of' simply links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical name for a partial or total failure of a person's recollection.

clue.text: Revises on the subject of flirts

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
a vamp is a seductive woman who flirts

explanation.surface: Someone redrafts a document about people who flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp something is to rework or renovate it, giving it a new and improved form.

clue.text: Subsequently, the second one lost time

indicators.note: the phrase has lost something, so a letter is removed from it

blocks.note: the latter is the second of two things mentioned
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A race report: the runner in second place wasted time.
explanation.walkthrough: LATTER drops one of its two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means afterwards or at a following time, a direct adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Bother and tease by twiddling cane

indicators.note: twiddling something turns it about, so those letters are fiddled into a new order

blocks.note: to tease is to irritate or annoy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pesters and irritates others by fiddling with a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, bother means irritation or nuisance, which is what an annoyance is.

clue.text: Sober seaman stops to accept promise of payment

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common sailor
to stem a flow is to stop it
an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A sailor stays off the drink in order to be offered an IOU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a verb acting on the seaman, but it is a synonym supplying letters, and 'to accept' means it takes the promise inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means moderate in eating and especially drinking, so sober and restrained.

clue.text: It's easy to describe earth, air, fire and water

definitions.text: to describe earth, air, fire and water
definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective relating to the classical elements

blocks.note: first meaning: simple, basic

blocks.clueFragment: to describe earth, air, fire and water
blocks.note: second meaning: relating to the four classical elements

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a boast that describing nature is simple; the two halves are separate senses of one adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both very simple or basic and, literally, of or relating to the elements of ancient philosophy.

clue.text: Begin again; go to the top left-hand corner!

definitions.text: go to the top left-hand corner
definitions.note: a whimsical second reading of the idiom

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for starting over

blocks.clueFragment: go to the top left-hand corner
blocks.note: second meaning: on a crossword grid, the first numbered square sits at the top left

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points to the playful literal reading: in a grid like this one, square number one is top left.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means returning to the starting point after a failure, and in a numbered grid the starting square is top left.

clue.text: Bush is misguidedly arrogant

indicators.note: something done misguidedly goes wrongly, so the following letters are set out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Bush, a former US president, is wrongly overbearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the US president's surname, but it means a shrubby plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is a bushy perennial herb grown for its aromatic leaves, so a small shrub.

clue.text: Ex-pupils' remedy don initially concealed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of that word is used

blocks.note: old boys, OBs, are former pupils of a school
a cure is a remedy
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A university lecturer hid the cure discovered by former students.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means hidden from view or made unclear, the same as concealed.

clue.text: Keen head creates a state of excitement

blocks.note: eager means keen
a ness is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic leader stirs everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss, but it is a headland: ness appears in British coastal names such as Sheerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerness is keen, impatient desire or enthusiasm, an excited state of wanting something.

clue.text: Failure to function over note on student irritation

blocks.note: G is a musical note
L for learner, the plate on a British learner driver's car
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A student annoyed by a note returned with a failing grade.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts the note above the student.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden minor malfunction, especially in equipment or software.

clue.text: Children are the prime concern

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring
second meaning: the main point under discussion

explanation.surface: A parent's declaration that the kids come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for offspring, and also the key matter or topic in a debate.

clue.text: Take no notice of disturbed region

indicators.note: something disturbed is moved out of place, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to disregard an area suffering unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is deliberately to pay them no attention, a direct verb phrase synonym.

clue.text: Maori GI involved in Japanese artistic creation

indicators.note: involved means intricately twisted, so the letters of the two words are tangled together

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A New Zealander and an American soldier take part in making something Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes and models.

clue.text: Some junior gynaecologists make up the party

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a portion of it, so the letters run across the word boundary

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A few young doctors form the group at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a wild, riotous party, typically with excessive drinking and indulgence.

clue.text: Direct behaviour

blocks.note: first meaning: to lead or manage, as with an orchestra
second meaning: the way a person acts

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it sounds like plain-speaking manners; the two words are separate meanings, one a verb and one a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means lead or manage; as a noun it means how someone behaves, as in good conduct.

clue.text: Fish eaten first is etiquette

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the preceding word is wanted

blocks.note: a cod is a fish
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Table manners dictate that the fish course comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A code of behaviour is a set of social rules, as in dress code, which is what etiquette is.

clue.text: Reptile in Greek capital hearing reverberation

indicators.note: the capital is the head letter, so only the first of that word is taken
hearing means the next word counts as it is heard, not as it is written

blocks.note: first letter of the word
a reverberation is an echo

explanation.surface: A lizard in Athens listens to sounds bouncing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek capital' tempts you towards Athens; it is just the initial letter of Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A gecko is a small nocturnal lizard of warm regions, known for climbing walls; lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Slip, for example, beneath the river

blocks.note: under means beneath
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: Someone slides under the water of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a verb for falling; it is the noun, a woman's undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a light garment worn under a dress, one example of the clothes worn beneath outer layers.
